title: On the Modular Isomorphism Problem for groups of class 3 and obelisks
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the Modular Isomorphism Problem (MIP) for finite p-groups: whether an isomorphism of modular group algebras kG and kH implies an isomorphism of the underlying groups G and H. The authors develop algebraic and group-theoretic techniques using the small group algebra, Jennings theory, and invariants derived from the lower central series and related quotients.

The paper proves new positive results for several families of p-groups, especially groups of nilpotency class 3 and certain 2-generated groups. It shows that, under specific structural conditions, the small group algebra determines the group up to isomorphism, and it also establishes invariance results for members of the lower central series for 2-generated class-3 groups with central exponent-p third commutator subgroup. The work further analyzes p-obelisks and exhibits an example of non-isomorphic groups with isomorphic small group algebras, showing limits of previously used strategies.

The setting is entirely mathematical and computational, focused on abstract finite p-groups and their modular group algebras rather than human participants or educational contexts. The main conclusion is that the small group algebra and related invariants resolve additional cases of the MIP, while also clarifying where existing methods fail.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a pure mathematics research article on the modular isomorphism problem for finite p-groups and modular group algebras. It does not study any educational technology intervention, K-12 population, or learning outcome.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational intervention, implementation, or learner outcome in this paper, so it has no direct impact on K-12 science inquiry or AI-supported education.
